title: Stream end without an own result is reported as success
description: `SDKExecutionSession._collect_turns()` is documented to return only after the dispatch’s own result, but the `result is None` branch only raises `ProviderError` when `turns.ledger.active` is true. If the stream ends after partial assistant text with no tracked background agent, `turns.own_result_seen` is still false and the method returns `turns.text()` as success with no WARNING/ERROR signal. `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py#test_dispatch_sends_query_and_collects_response` and similar no-`ResultMessage` streams assert this partial text as success, so the failure mode has no observable signal test. A peer disconnect or truncated CLI stream can therefore produce a successful dispatch with incomplete output. Raise whenever the stream ends before `own_result_seen`, log the failure, and add a test asserting the observable signal.

title: Numeric config reads still accept bool values
description: The added comment says “bool before int: bool is a subclass of int,” but only the `type_ is bool` branch rejects wrong types; the `type_ is int` branch still uses `isinstance(value, int)`, which accepts `True`/`False`, and the numeric fallback accepts `bool` through `(int, float)`. A TOML value such as `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s = true` therefore reaches `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py#_background_idle_timeout_s` as `True`, which `asyncio.timeout()` treats as one second instead of failing fast. `tests/config/test_manager.py#test_typed_read_rejects_non_bool` covers the inverse case only. Reject `bool` explicitly for `int`/`float` reads and add parameterized type-validation tests.

title: Review settings policy relies on a type annotation instead of validation
description: `ReviewTemplate.setting_sources` is now declared non-`None` in `src/squadron/review/templates/__init__.py:36`, but `run_review_with_profile()` simply forwards `template.setting_sources` when there is no override. `src/squadron/providers/sdk/provider.py:89-90` then omits `setting_sources` entirely for `None`, and `src/squadron/providers/sdk/settings.py:4-6` documents that an unset value loads user settings. Several changed/remaining tests still construct templates with `setting_sources=None` — for example `tests/review/test_templates.py:186`, `tests/review/test_review_client.py:35`, and `tests/cli/test_review_profile.py:21` — so a direct `ReviewTemplate` can still bypass the D10 policy and inherit the operator’s user `CLAUDE.md`/settings. Validate or default `setting_sources` at the `run_review_with_profile()` boundary and update hand-built templates to the non-`None` contract.

title: Async SDK paths perform synchronous config file I/O on the event loop
description: New async code calls synchronous `get_typed_config()` directly: `open_pipeline_session()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:457-460`, `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py:144-153`, and the background-wait path via `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py#_background_idle_timeout_s`. `src/squadron/config/manager.py#_read_toml` performs `open()`/`tomllib.load()` disk I/O and parsing. The Python rules require synchronous work inside `async def` to be under 1 ms or offloaded; disk-backed config reads and TOML parsing cannot guarantee that and can block all other loop work. Preload/cache settings before entering the async path or use `asyncio.to_thread()`/an injected settings object.

title: Background wait concurrency has no load-tier coverage
description: The new dispatch path adds network-stream waiting, idle timers, cancellation/timeout behavior, and background-task state on a persistent SDK client. The diff adds unit coverage in `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py#TestBackgroundIdleTimeout` using 0.15-second scripts and functional assertions, but no changed `tests/load/` case accompanies the slice. The Python/load-test rule requires a realistic load test for network/concurrency/environment-layer changes, asserting latency, throughput, or resource bounds; unit tests with small sleeps do not catch event-loop starvation, leaked stream iterators, or timer contention. Add a `tests/load/` case with many concurrent/progressing/silent background agents and gate it in CI.

title: Unusable sessions can still be touched through `capture_summary`
description: `_require_usable()` is enforced at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:420-421` and called first in `dispatch()`, `compact()`, and `seed_context()`, but not in `set_model()` or `capture_summary()`. After `_reconnect()` fails, it sets `current_model = None`; if a later summary capture supplies `summary_model`, `capture_summary()` calls `set_model()` on the dead client before `dispatch()` can fail fast. `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py#test_failed_reconnect_marks_session_unusable` checks only `dispatch()`, `compact()`, and `seed_context()` after the failure. Add the guard to `set_model()`/`capture_summary()` and cover a summary path with a model alias after failed rotation.

title: Telemetry and digest comments contradict the new always-present metadata
description: `_dispatch_via_agent()` still says “tool_telemetry is empty when the run had no tools,” but `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry()` now starts from `describe_run_settings()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py:174`, and its docstring at `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py:104-109` correctly says prompt/settings keys are always present. `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/summary.py#_execute_summary` also still says its telemetry variable is empty unless a non-SDK run had tools. Separately, `src/squadron/review/models.py:214-216` says `None` renders as “not reported,” while `src/squadron/review/persistence.py#_render_optional` uses `_NOT_COMPUTED = "not computed"` and `tests/review/test_persistence.py#TestPromptAndSettingsDigestLines` asserts that sentinel. Update these comments to distinguish “tool keys absent” from “prompt/settings keys always present,” and fix the sentinel wording.

title: Settings-policy test helper swallows all exceptions
description: `_capture_config()` defines `_Captured` at `tests/providers/sdk/test_settings_policy.py:27` but wraps the whole path in `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` at line 40. This is a blanket catch with no logging or re-raise; unexpected exceptions from the path can be hidden as long as a config was recorded first. The Python rules require either a specific caught type with justification, a logged/re-raised handler, or a documented process-boundary handler. Use a narrow sentinel, catch only `_Captured`, or return a fake agent instead of raising, so unrelated test failures remain visible.

title: Reject booleans when reading integer config values
description: Description: `bool` is a subclass of `int`, so `get_typed_config(..., int)` accepts a TOML boolean for an integer key. For example, setting `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s = true` can be treated as a one-second timeout instead of producing a type error. Explicitly exclude booleans from the integer check.

title: Detect an explicitly empty system prompt on the session path
description: Description: The session-path guard checks the truthiness of `context.params.get("system_prompt")`. A step that explicitly supplies `system_prompt: ""` bypasses the guard, even though the session cannot apply a per-step prompt and the action will silently use the session prompt instead. Check whether the parameter is present, rather than whether its value is truthy.

title: Check session usability before changing its model
description: Description: A failed reconnect sets `unusable_reason`, but `set_model()` does not check it. The session dispatch path calls `set_model()` before `dispatch()`, so a later step can attempt an SDK operation on the failed client before reaching the usability check, potentially masking the recorded reconnect failure. Require usability before invoking the client.

title: Escape agent text before rendering it as Rich markup
description: Description: This appends agent-generated text to `ActionResult.error`. The CLI later interpolates that error into `rprint` markup in `src/squadron/cli/commands/run.py:561`, so markup in the response tail can alter terminal rendering or trigger markup parsing errors. Escape the agent text or render the error as plain text.

title: Add a load test for SDK background waiting
description: Description: This change adds a network-backed async stream-waiting and task-stopping path, but the existing `tests/load/` suite has no coverage for SDK dispatches. Add a load test that exercises realistic background-task waiting and checks a resource or latency bound, as required for network and concurrency paths.
